values.value: The named target sits on Salesforce Core, and there is no Salesforce footprint to sit it on. A platform-precursor project — org, licences, user model, governance — has to land before any marketing migration can be scheduled, and it is a different budget line with a different sponsor. Raise it now rather than at contracting: it is the single most common reason an otherwise-ready migration slips a quarter.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/skills/10-roadmap.md — "ORG MODEL & TEAM ... governance framework, permission architecture, DevOps pipeline"; and the MCE+ SKU / org-model dependencies called out under external dependencies. TARGET LIST NARROWED TO sfmc_next, and for two independent reasons, either of which alone would be enough. First the predicate: core_footprint is declared only in instrument/migration-accelerator/supplements/mcn_readiness.yaml, and that set is fired only by packs whose target is sfmc_next (instrument/migration-accelerator/pairs/any_to_mcn.yaml, hubspot_to_mcn.yaml, sfmc_to_mcn.yaml). No classic-MCE pack fires it — eloqua_to_sfmc.yaml declares no supplement sets and hubspot_to_sfmc.yaml fires sfmc_classic_readiness plus hubspot_context — so on an sfmc target the clause could only ever be false and the gate was dead. Second the readout: skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/framework-reference.md — "Marketing Cloud Connect -> Native Salesforce Core integration (Retired). MCN is on Core" — is a statement about Marketing Cloud NEXT. Classic Marketing Cloud Engagement is not Core-native; it reaches Core through Marketing Cloud Connect, so "the named target sits on Salesforce Core" would have been false had the gate ever fired on sfmc. Both faults are removed by the same edit: the gate now fires only where its predicate is answerable and its prose is true.
